title: O Spirit of the Living God
description: O Spirit of the Living God in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 587, “The Kingdom of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Spir-it of the liv-ing God, In all Thy plen-i-tude of grace, Wher-e'er the foot of man hath trod, De-scend on our be-night-ed race!

lines: O Spirit of the living God,
In all Thy plenitude of grace,
Where'er the foot of man hath trod,
Be darkness, at Thy coming, light;
Souls without strength inspire with might;
O spirit of the Lord! prepare
All the round earth her God to meet;
Breathe Thou abroad like morning air,
Till hearts of stone begin to beat.
Baptize the nations; far and nigh
The triumphs of the cross record;
Till every people call Thee Lord.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
